column3: “The Council members” and “the apostles” make the Greek pronouns explicit; the first verb literally pictures being sawn through.
The Greek identifies the men without separately naming apostles.
“Claiming to be somebody” renders the Greek “saying he was somebody”; the Greek counts men explicitly.
The Greek says “now I say,” rather than specifically “in the present case I advise.”
Their being persuaded by him is already in this Greek verse; BSB moves it to the next.
The agreement with Gamaliel is in the preceding Greek verse; “Gamaliel” supplies the pronoun’s referent.
